chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Express our hadith clearly, for we are an eloquent people.'

key_terms.أَعْرِبُوا: express clearly in proper Arabic; apply correct grammatical vocalization (i'rab) — imperative of Form IV root ع-ر-ب
key_terms.حَدِيثَنَا: our hadith; the transmitted sayings of the Imams (AS) — first person plural possessive, emphasizing the Imam's direct ownership of the speech
key_terms.فُصَحَاءُ: eloquent people; masters of Arabic speech — plural of فَصِيح, denoting those possessing fasaha (highest linguistic clarity)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instruct regarding the proper transmission of his hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) commands those who transmit his hadith to convey them with proper Arabic eloquence and grammatical precision (i'rab), rather than in a garbled or metrically imprecise form. The verb أَعْرِبُوا — from the root ع-ر-ب — carries the dual sense of 'speak/write correctly in Arabic' and 'apply proper vowelization,' while the justification فَإِنَّا قَوْمٌ فُصَحَاءُ anchors the command in the Imam's God-given linguistic mastery as a member of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Express our<sup>asws</sup> Ahadeeth in a clear manner; for we<sup>asws</sup> are an eloquent people’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following.
“Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said, ‘Speak our Hadith clearly because we are eloquent people.’”
